title: Regime-Switching and Deep Learning: A State-Dependent Early Warning System for Volatility Transitions in a Frontier Market
content: Frontier financial markets  face a persistent diagnostic gap in forecasting volatility: traditional linear and single regime GARCH models fail to capture structural breaks, nonlinear spillovers, and regime transitions that define fragile market dynamics. In particular, ARMA–FIGARCH specifications could not exhaust residual linear persistence, motivating the integration of Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks to close this gap. This limitation leaves policymakers without timely, actionable signals to anticipate systemic stress. To address this gap, this study developed a hybrid Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) neural network combined with Fractionally Integrated GARCH (FIGARCH) econometric filtering to design a regime sensitive early warning system (EWS)  in a frontier financial market. Using daily data from the NSE 20 Share Index, USD/KES exchange rate, and Brent crude volatility spanning 2000–2025 forecasting horizons were first assessed, showing that one day signals were overly reactive and ten day forecasts diluted precision, while five day predictions achieved the strongest balance with 98% accuracy and robust detection across Calm (F1 = 0.99), Moderate (F1 = 0.82), and Stress (F1 = 0.69) regimes. Econometric validation confirmed that conditional heteroskedasticity was adequately captured by the FIGARCH specification, though residual autocorrelation required AR refinements to improve model fit. Building on these diagnostics, probabilistic stress thresholds were developed to translate regime signals into actionable alarms, distinguishing transitional phases from full stress episodes and providing regulators with a practical buffer for intervention. The hybrid model thus advances methodological innovation by combining long memory volatility modelling with deep learning adaptability, while delivering Basel-compliant tail-risk alarms and a state-dependent policy matrix for regulators, offering policy relevant tools for monitoring volatility and crisis preparedness. The findings underscore the importance of regime sensitive approaches in frontier markets, offering credible and timely signals to anticipate and mitigate systemic stress, and contributing to both academic literature and practical financial stability oversight.
